title: Ringed active nematic replicates on seed 3: 25 persistent splits, gen 4, 53 tracks >= 1 BL; surfactant ring rim/core 1.49 (89/130 membrane-like) vs 0.93 (0/130) with chis=0
summary: Fresh seed 3, t=1000. Dynamics are those of the parent colony (the surfactant is passive): rods nucleate from noise, swim and divide, 46 splits, 25 persistent, generation 4, 53 tracks >= 1 BL (max 3.4). labkit radial surfactant s: peak at rho=0.75, rim/core 1.49, rim/outside 2.1, 89/130 individuals membrane-like. chis=0 on the same seed (identical rods, same splits): s peaks at the core, rim/core 0.93, 0/130 membrane-like. Tracks #7, #27, #14, #64 (rerun/tracks.png) are rods followed for 300-850 t.

observations.B: rerun/FACTS.md: surfactant rim/core 1.49, rim/outside 2.1, 89/130 membrane-like; chis0/FACTS.md 0.93, 0/130

controls_run.M: zeta=0 arm of the parent, seed 3, in 20261025T1049-c01-review-nematic/zeta0

verdicts.limitation: The ring is a passive adsorption layer of a surfactant that does not act back, so it adds organization but no function; aggregate rim/core 1.49 sits at the 1.5 threshold on this seed (89/130 individuals pass). Motion is short (max 3.4 BL). I did not follow track 46 of seed 2 (the claim's track) or check resolution, and the parent's founder nucleation fails at 1.5x on seed 3 (my review 20261025T1140-c01-review-nematic-res15).
